clue.text: Succeed in tunnelling?

parts.note: a phrase for completing a task, read literally as boring one's way right through the earth

explanation.surface: A question about whether a tunneller will make it through.
explanation.definitionFit: To persist with a plan to its finish is to succeed; a tunneller literally passes right through the rock.

clue.text: Trying to get the feel of things

definitions.text: Trying to get the feel of things

parts.words: Trying to get the feel of things
parts.note: read figuratively as feeling one's way towards understanding, and literally as fumbling about with the hands in the dark

explanation.surface: Someone new to a job is getting used to it.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling blindly about with the hands is a literal search by touch, also used of tentative attempts to understand.

clue.text: Stuff the flower

definitions.meaning: stuff is an old word for woven cloth, here a rough woollen fabric
a flower is something that flows, a river: the one on the English-Scottish border

explanation.surface: Fill the bloom with something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' is a crossword convention for a river (it flows). The Tweed is the river forming part of the border between England and Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Tweed is a woollen cloth, and the Tweed is a river on the Scottish border.

clue.text: Banished ambassador who was overdrawn

indicators.note: the ambassador who was in the red is placed inside the word for overdrawn

parts.note: an overdrawn account is in the red
a legate is a papal envoy or ambassador

explanation.surface: An envoy who ran up debts was sent away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'who was' is the container signal: the ambassador ends up inside the overdrawn word, since a British overdrawn account is said to be 'in the red'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being relegated means being demoted or sent down to a lower place, akin to exile.

clue.text: Steal the show from someone else away from the footlights

definitions.text: Steal the show from someone else
definitions.meaning: to outshine another performer and take the attention
towards the back of the stage, far from the front lights and audience

explanation.surface: An actor hogs attention though positioned at the back of the stage.
explanation.walkthrough: A verb and an adverb share one spelling: an actor at the back makes the others turn away from the audience, hence the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Theatrical sense: the rear of the stage, and drawing the attention from fellow performers.

clue.text: Port had been removed from the top of the car

indicators.note: removed suggests the letters have been moved about into a new order

explanation.surface: A drink has been taken off the car's roof.
explanation.walkthrough: 'been removed' signals an anagram of PORT HAD; the surface wants the port wine to vanish.
explanation.definitionFit: A rigid fixed roof on a motor vehicle, as opposed to a soft folding one.

clue.text: Dot two I's, seems strange to a fool

indicators.note: the letters given appear strange, rearranged into another word

parts.note: two copies of the letter I

explanation.surface: Instructions to dot two letters strike a simpleton as odd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seems strange' signals an anagram of DOT plus II (two I's).
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a stupid person or simpleton.

clue.text: One being indecisive when the rota is revised

indicators.note: a revised rota is rearranged, so these three words' letters are reshuffled

explanation.surface: Someone dithers whenever the duty roster is changed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revised' signals an anagram of THE ROTA IS.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who hesitates is unable to make up their mind.

clue.text: Crime of a boy underneath most of the woody growth

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece placed underneath another follows it
most of a word means its final letter is cut off

parts.note: a tree is a tall woody plant
a son is a male child

explanation.surface: A youngster commits an offence beneath the shrubbery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' cuts TREE to TRE; 'underneath' puts A SON below it in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Betrayal of one's country or sovereign is the gravest offence in law.

clue.text: Ringed spot of colour round small room of limited use

parts.note: a round shape is the letter O
a cell is a small room, as in a prison or monastery
U/S is short for unserviceable, i.e. useless

explanation.surface: A coloured circle surrounds a little room that serves almost no purpose.
explanation.walkthrough: US (from U/S, unserviceable) is British slang for useless.
explanation.definitionFit: Zoology term: an eye-like marking, as on a peacock's feather or butterfly wing.

clue.text: Reprint sure is developing the point

indicators.note: letters still developing have not yet settled into their final order

parts.note: a point of the compass, here east

explanation.surface: An editor confirms a new printing is turning out to be the main issue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'developing' signals an anagram of SURE IS, giving REISSU; then E, east, a compass point.
explanation.definitionFit: A second publication of a book or record already issued once.

clue.text: In archaeological excavation, name worker showing scorn

parts.note: a dig is an archaeological excavation site
an ant is the classic crossword worker

explanation.surface: At a dig, a labourer is named and reacts with contempt.
explanation.definitionFit: Angry at perceived unfairness, which shows contempt for what caused it.

clue.text: Paul's companion found American bird first!

indicators.note: the bird is put first, ahead of the American abbreviation

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird
US is short for United States, so American

explanation.surface: An excited claim that a US bird was spotted ahead of others.
explanation.walkthrough: Titus was a companion of St Paul and the recipient of one of his New Testament letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Biblical figure: a Greek follower of Paul who travelled with him.

clue.text: Rubbish in the entrance-it's enough to take one's breath away

definitions.text: it's enough to take one's breath away

indicators.note: the rubbish goes inside the word for entrance

parts.note: a gate is an entrance to a field or garden
rot means nonsense or rubbish

explanation.surface: A heap of junk at the gateway is a breathtaking sight.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on 'breathtaking': the answer is a strangling cord that literally stops breathing.
explanation.definitionFit: A cord or wire used to strangle a victim literally cuts off breathing.

clue.text: Criminal on court?

definitions.meaning: a gangster engaged in extortion or fraud
a whimsical sense: someone with a bat for tennis or squash playing on a court

explanation.surface: Is the wrongdoer facing a judge?
explanation.walkthrough: 'court' suggests a law court for a criminal, but it is a tennis or squash court.
explanation.definitionFit: A gangster running a fraud, and jokingly a player wielding a bat on court.

clue.text: Play upon words about girl being a very strict person

indicators.note: the wordplay term goes about, surrounding, the girl's name

parts.note: a pun is a play on words
Rita is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A joke about a young woman shows she is very prim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the container signal, wrapping the pun round the girl; 'Play upon words' looks like part of the surface story but is the one piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with rigid moral or religious standards, after the 17th-century Protestant sect.

clue.text: No-one goes all the way in this contest

definitions.text: No-one goes all the way in this contest

parts.words: No-one goes all the way in this contest
parts.note: a race where each runner covers only one stage before handing on the baton

explanation.surface: Nobody completes the full course in this competition.
explanation.definitionFit: Team running event in which each member covers one leg, passing a baton.

clue.text: The first Scotsman on the road?

definitions.text: The first Scotsman on the road?

parts.words: The first Scotsman on the road?
parts.note: the first man in Genesis given a Scottish Mac- prefix, naming the road surface invented by a Scot

explanation.surface: A question about which Scot first travelled the highway.
explanation.walkthrough: The road surface is named after John McAdam, a Scottish engineer; read as Mac plus Adam, the first man.
explanation.definitionFit: A road surface of compacted broken stone, named after its Scottish inventor.

clue.text: Speed of Russian flier to leave the country

indicators.note: the speed belongs to the flier, so the plane comes before the speed

parts.note: a MiG is a Russian fighter plane
rate means speed

explanation.surface: How fast a Soviet jet must fly to escape abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: To move from one region or nation to settle in another, as birds do seasonally.

clue.text: Unintended motorway hazard?

parts.note: an unintentional error, read whimsically as fog on a major road plus an extra syllable

explanation.surface: An accidental danger on a major road.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as MIST, a fog hazard on motorways, the clue hints at the word for an unintended error.
explanation.definitionFit: An error is something done unintentionally.

clue.text: Unit of heat, one of many counted by a weight-watcher

definitions.meaning: the energy needed to warm a gram of water by one degree

definitions.text: one of many counted by a weight-watcher
definitions.meaning: dieters tally the energy content of their food

explanation.surface: A heat measure that slimmers keep careful tally of.
explanation.definitionFit: A physics energy unit, and the food-energy measure dieters count.

clue.text: Musicians union

parts.note: read as a trade union, it is really a coming together of players to perform, or agreement

explanation.surface: The trade body representing performers of music.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical performance unites players, and 'in concert' means in agreement or united.

clue.text: Gone out with Tex performing in court

indicators.note: performing suggests the letters doing tricks, rearranged

explanation.surface: A man called Tex left after appearing before a judge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'performing' signals an anagram of TEX, giving EXT; IN and CT (court) follow. The surface pictures Tex on stage, but 'performing' only shuffles him.
explanation.definitionFit: A fire or species no longer alive or burning has died out.

clue.text: A shade inexperienced

explanation.surface: A slightly naive person.
explanation.definitionFit: A colour on the spectrum, and a word for raw or naive novices.

clue.text: First sly pupil leaves being conspicuous

annotationWithheld.why: First sly pupil leaves being conspicuous (5) as held: no parse of the wordplay gives NOISY; clue likely garbled in OCR and no source found
annotationWithheld.clue: First sly pupil leaves being conspicuous

clue.text: Sailing boat beached?

parts.note: a stranded vessel is the surface reading, but it is a wheeled craft that sails on the shore

explanation.surface: A yacht has run aground.
explanation.definitionFit: A wheeled land vehicle with a sail, raced on beaches.

clue.text: Man, he somehow got out of crashed vehicle

indicators.note: a crashed vehicle is wrecked, its letters jumbled once the other word is taken out

explanation.surface: A man somehow climbed out of the wrecked car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'he somehow got out of' takes H and E from VEHICLE; 'crashed' scrambles the remaining VICLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A male first name, an example of a man.

clue.text: Lady identifies herselfin the States

parts.note: a woman introducing herself says 'I am ...'; the printed run-together 'herselfin' is 'herself in', the 'in' a link
Erica is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A woman introduces herself while in the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: The lady introduces herself as '(I) am Erica', so her words come before her name. 'herselfin' is a print slip for 'herself in'.
explanation.definitionFit: The United States is commonly called by the continent's name.

clue.text: It alone could bring joy

indicators.note: the words could be rearranged to bring out a new word

explanation.surface: Solitude by itself can make one happy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could bring' signals an anagram of IT ALONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: great happiness or exhilaration.

clue.text: Ancient village appreciated by tradesmen

definitions.meaning: paying a bill promptly pleases suppliers

explanation.surface: Traders welcome an old hamlet.
explanation.definitionFit: An old community founded in antiquity, and prompt payment of an account.
